findings.title: HTML cannot be cached by the CDN (no-store / private)
findings.evidence: Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate; CDN cache status on two requests: MISS / MISS
findings.why: Every visit forces the server to rebuild the page from scratch, which slows the first byte for every user and hurts Core Web Vitals. This is sometimes intentional (carts, logged-in areas) — confirm before changing.
findings.fix: Remove the setting that forces dynamic rendering (for Next.js: force-dynamic, or cookies()/headers() in server components) or enable revalidation so the CDN can cache HTML. Verify: repeat requests should show a cache HIT.

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.why: Security headers protect visitors. They are not a direct ranking factor but show a well-maintained site.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers in your hosting or CDN configuration; start Content-Security-Policy in Report-Only mode.

what_works: One canonical host: https://techand.ai 301-redirects to https://www.techand.ai
Every live page is listed in the sitemap
Site serves Markdown to AI agents on request
All 11 search and AI crawlers tested (GPTBot, ClaudeBot, PerplexityBot, Googlebot and more) receive the full page
probe.note: AI crawler checks use the crawler user-agent only; real crawlers are also verified by IP, so a pass here means no user-agent based blocking.

findings.title: Malformed sameAs profile link
findings.why: A broken identity link is worse than none: it confuses entity matching in Google and AI systems.
findings.fix: Remove or correct the invalid entry and link only real, active profiles.

findings.title: Few verified profiles linked in sameAs
findings.why: Entity recognition works best with 4-6 independent profiles (LinkedIn, directories, Wikidata, Crunchbase, review sites).
findings.fix: Add sameAs links to every real business profile.

findings.title: Structured contact details are thinner than what the site shows
findings.evidence: Missing in schema: streetAddress, addressLocality, telephone, email
findings.why: Search engines cannot match your business listing to your site when the address and phone in schema are incomplete.
findings.fix: Add full PostalAddress (streetAddress, addressLocality, addressRegion, postalCode, addressCountry), telephone and email to Organization schema.

findings.title: No alternateName in Organization schema
findings.why: Helps search engines and AI map spelling variants of the brand to one entity.
findings.fix: Add alternateName with common variants of the brand name.

findings.title: Organization schema has no @id
findings.why: An @id lets other schema (Service, Article) reference the same organisation cleanly.
findings.fix: Add "@id": "https://techand.ai/#organization".

findings.title: Experience claim conflicts with the founding date
findings.evidence: "20+ years" on https://www.techand.ai/ but schema foundingDate is 2020
findings.why: Contradictory facts damage trust with buyers and with search quality systems.
findings.fix: Make the claims consistent (e.g. "leadership with 20+ years of experience") or correct the founding date.

findings.title: Service pages have no Service schema
findings.why: Service schema tells search engines exactly what you offer, where and by whom, and separates similar service pages.
findings.fix: Add Service JSON-LD (serviceType, provider → Organization @id, areaServed) on each service page.

findings.title: No BreadcrumbList schema
findings.why: Breadcrumbs show site hierarchy in search results and help search engines understand structure.
findings.fix: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to every inner page.

findings.title: Articles have no named human author
findings.why: Expertise signals (E-E-A-T) depend on a real, credentialed author, especially on advice or compliance topics.
findings.fix: Credit a named expert with an author page, job title and LinkedIn (author @type Person with url and sameAs).

findings.title: No freshness signal on articles
findings.evidence: 2 of 2 sampled articles have dateModified equal to datePublished
findings.why: Time-sensitive content looks unmaintained without a genuine update date.
findings.fix: Show a visible "Last reviewed" date and update dateModified only after real edits.

findings.title: Homepage H1 does not name the business or what it does
findings.evidence: Homepage H1: "Value Driven Innovation through Automation"
findings.why: The homepage H1 is the strongest on-page signal of who you are, what you sell and where.
findings.fix: Rewrite the H1 to name the brand, the service category and the location.

findings.title: Contact form is not in the server-rendered HTML
findings.evidence: Raw HTML of https://www.techand.ai/contact-us has 0 <form> and 0 <input> elements
findings.why: Crawlers and AI agents that do not run JavaScript see no way to contact you.
findings.fix: Server-render the form (fields, labels, submit) or add a <noscript> fallback form.

findings.title: Images without width and height
findings.evidence: 76 images on sampled pages lack explicit dimensions
findings.why: Images without reserved space can shift the layout while loading (CLS).
findings.fix: Add width and height (or aspect-ratio) to every image.

findings.title: Phone number in a link but not shown on the page
findings.why: Hidden or unlabeled numbers can be picked up by directories and AI as conflicting contact details.
findings.fix: Confirm the number, display it, or remove the link.

findings.title: No speculation rules for instant navigation
findings.why: Prefetching likely next pages makes navigation feel instant.
findings.fix: Add conservative speculation rules for key pages (e.g. contact and top services).

extra_findings.why: Claims to deliver Microsoft products need proof such as Solutions Partner designation, to be credible to enterprise and banking buyers.

extra_findings.title: Case study and testimonial proof is thin
extra_findings.evidence: The homepage teaser "How Customer Service Teams Are Achieving a 20% to 45% Increase in…" is cut off. No client names, quotes or reviews appear in the supplied text.
extra_findings.why: A percentage without a named client or source reads as unsubstantiated. Enterprise buyers in the UAE look for reference clients.
extra_findings.fix: Publish named case studies with the client, scope, timeline and measurable results. Add testimonials, logos and third-party reviews such as Clutch or Gartner Peer Insights.

extra_findings.title: Service pages are generic and duplicated
extra_findings.evidence: Every /whatwedo/ page repeats the same block: "We guide your business through every step of technology growth to ensure you stay ahead of competitors." Each page also carries the same "Assess & Envision" copy. Managed Services is described as "Expert IT management for your daily needs".
extra_findings.why: Duplicated boilerplate and generic descriptions give each page little unique value. The pages lack timelines, deliverables and UAE specifics.
extra_findings.fix: Write unique content per service: scope, methodology, typical timelines, deliverables, SLAs, a UAE example and FAQs.

extra_findings.title: Heavy repeated mega-menu text on every page
extra_findings.evidence: The same navigation text, from "Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations UAE" to "Predictive Models", precedes the content on every page.
extra_findings.why: It dilutes the unique content, and the menu shows up as page text. Menu labels also look keyword-stuffed ("…UAE" repeated).
extra_findings.fix: Make the navigation less crawlable-noisy and the labels more natural. Make sure the main content comes first in the HTML.

extra_findings.title: Formatting artifact and only high-commitment CTAs
extra_findings.evidence: "Let's discuss how we can help your business" shows a raw HTML entity. CTAs are "Talk to Sales", "Call Now" and "Request Call Back".
extra_findings.why: The artifact looks unpolished. There is no low-friction option such as a guide, assessment or pricing guidance.
extra_findings.fix: Fix the entity encoding. Add softer CTAs such as a readiness checklist, a sample scope or a downloadable guide.

extra_findings.title: No pricing or engagement-model guidance, and no leadership info
extra_findings.evidence: No pricing, ranges, or engagement models appear on the service pages. No team or leadership names appear in the text supplied.
extra_findings.why: Buyers can't qualify the cost. Anonymity lowers trust.
extra_findings.fix: Add indicative engagement models, typical project durations, and a leadership/team page.

site_audit.score_cap_reason: 1 critical issue found — score capped at 70 until fixed

findings.title: Broken pages (4xx, 5xx or timeout)
findings.why: Pages that return errors waste crawl budget and lose any ranking signals pointing to them.
findings.fix: Fix or 301-redirect broken URLs to the most relevant live page.

findings.title: www and non-www versions are not consolidated
findings.why: If both versions do not resolve to one canonical host, links and signals are split.
findings.fix: Make the www version redirect (301) to the main domain with a valid certificate for both hostnames.

findings.title: HTML cannot be cached by the CDN (no-store / private)
findings.evidence: Cache-Control: private, no-cache, no-store, max-age=0, must-revalidate; CDN cache status on two requests: MISS / MISS
findings.why: Every visit forces the server to rebuild the page from scratch, which slows the first byte for every user and hurts Core Web Vitals. This is sometimes intentional (carts, logged-in areas) — confirm before changing.
findings.fix: Remove the setting that forces dynamic rendering (for Next.js: force-dynamic, or cookies()/headers() in server components) or enable revalidation so the CDN can cache HTML. Verify: repeat requests should show a cache HIT.

findings.title: Malformed sameAs profile link
findings.why: A broken identity link is worse than none: it confuses entity matching in Google and AI systems.
findings.fix: Remove or correct the invalid entry and link only real, active profiles.

findings.title: Structured contact details are thinner than what the site shows
findings.evidence: Missing in schema: streetAddress, addressLocality, telephone, email
findings.why: Search engines cannot match your business listing to your site when the address and phone in schema are incomplete.
findings.fix: Add full PostalAddress (streetAddress, addressLocality, addressRegion, postalCode, addressCountry), telephone and email to Organization schema.

findings.title: Experience claim conflicts with the founding date
findings.evidence: "20+ years" on https://www.techand.ai/ but schema foundingDate is 2020
findings.why: Contradictory facts damage trust with buyers and with search quality systems.
findings.fix: Make the claims consistent (e.g. "leadership with 20+ years of experience") or correct the founding date.

findings.title: Service pages have no Service schema
findings.why: Service schema tells search engines exactly what you offer, where and by whom, and separates similar service pages.
findings.fix: Add Service JSON-LD (serviceType, provider → Organization @id, areaServed) on each service page.

findings.title: No BreadcrumbList schema
findings.why: Breadcrumbs show site hierarchy in search results and help search engines understand structure.
findings.fix: Add BreadcrumbList JSON-LD to every inner page.

findings.title: The site does not rank in Google’s top 10 for any keyword
findings.evidence: Top-10 rankings in United Arab Emirates: techand.ai 0 vs competitor median 381 (theknowledgeacademy.com, youglish.com, boardroom-ai.ae)
findings.why: Without top-10 rankings the site gets almost no organic traffic, however good the pages are.
findings.fix: Build authority first (partner listings, directories, reviews, mentions) and target long-tail keywords where competitors are weak.

findings.title: Organic traffic is under 10% of competitors
findings.evidence: Estimated monthly organic visits: techand.ai 0 vs competitor median 9,897
findings.why: Most searchers in this market are going to competitors.
findings.fix: Close the keyword and backlink gaps shown in this report.

findings.title: Very young domain competing with long-established sites
findings.evidence: techand.ai registered 2026-02-19 (0.6 years) vs competitor median 14.2 years
findings.why: New domains have little accumulated trust; on-page fixes alone rarely move competitive terms in the first year.
findings.fix: Invest in off-site entity building (partner directories, reviews, mentions) and target long-tail, lower-difficulty searches first.

findings.title: Keyword gap: searches competitors win and you do not
findings.evidence: 25 keywords where competitors rank in the top 10 and you are not in the top 20. Top: "vertically" (9900/mo), "employees" (8100/mo), "typewriting centre near me" (6600/mo), "closes" (6600/mo), "console google cloud platform" (4400/mo)
findings.why: Each of these is proven demand in your market that is currently going to competitors.
findings.fix: Create or improve a dedicated page for the highest-volume, lowest-difficulty gap keywords first.

findings.title: Far fewer referring domains than competitors
findings.why: Links from other websites are one of the strongest ranking signals; competitors are far ahead.
findings.fix: Earn links from partner directories, industry associations, suppliers, press and guest content.

findings.title: Unproven scale and financial claims on contact page
findings.evidence: "We bring together a massive team of experts and significant financial backing to ensure your project succeeds on time."
findings.why: The claim is vague and unverifiable. It gives no headcount, funding source or delivery record. Readers and quality raters read this as filler, and it weakens trust.
findings.fix: Replace it with verifiable facts: team size, years operating, number of projects delivered, and named leadership. Add a link to proof.

findings.title: No named authors or expert bylines on insight articles
findings.evidence: The articles on D365 F&O reporting and Peppol e-invoicing show only "Dynamics 365 7 min read", with no author name or credentials shown.
findings.why: Technical and finance-compliance content (UAE e-invoicing, consolidation) is YMYL-adjacent. Without a named expert, the experience and expertise signals are weak.
findings.fix: Add bylines with bios, roles, Microsoft certifications and LinkedIn links. Add reviewer and last-updated dates.

findings.title: Partner status and certifications not evidenced
findings.evidence: Pages list many Dynamics 365, Copilot and Azure OpenAI services, but the text shows no Microsoft partner badge, competencies or certifications.
findings.why: Claims to deliver Microsoft products need proof such as Solutions Partner designation, to be credible to enterprise and banking buyers.
findings.fix: Show Microsoft partner badges, designations, MCT/consultant certifications and links to the Partner directory listing in the footer and on the Why Tech& page.

findings.title: Case study and testimonial proof is thin
findings.evidence: The homepage teaser "How Customer Service Teams Are Achieving a 20% to 45% Increase in…" is cut off. No client names, quotes or reviews appear in the supplied text.
findings.why: A percentage without a named client or source reads as unsubstantiated. Enterprise buyers in the UAE look for reference clients.
findings.fix: Publish named case studies with the client, scope, timeline and measurable results. Add testimonials, logos and third-party reviews such as Clutch or Gartner Peer Insights.

findings.title: ChatGPT recommends other providers, not you
findings.evidence: For "I need to choose a provider. Which are the best ai in cloud company United Arab Emirates? Give me up to 8 companies with…" ChatGPT listed: nxaara.com, nexait.ai, oracle.com, ae.scc.com, cloud.netcity.ae, themiddleeast.cloud
findings.why: Buyers increasingly ask AI assistants for shortlists; not being named means not being considered.
findings.fix: Get listed where AI answers draw their sources: the directories and review sites cited (nxaara.com, nexait.ai, oracle.com, ae.scc.com), plus comparison and "best X" pages that name you.

findings.title: Perplexity recommends other providers, not you
findings.evidence: For "I need to choose a provider. Which are the best ai in cloud company United Arab Emirates? Give me up to 8 companies with…" Perplexity listed: g42.ai, core42.ai, presight.ai, aiqintelligence.ae, ai71.ai, nodeshift.cloud
findings.why: Buyers increasingly ask AI assistants for shortlists; not being named means not being considered.
findings.fix: Get listed where AI answers draw their sources: the directories and review sites cited (f6s.com, lumitech.co, sortlist.com, revenuebase.ai), plus comparison and "best X" pages that name you.

findings.title: Site does not rank at the top for its own brand name
findings.evidence: Search "tech&": your position not in top 20
findings.why: If people cannot find you by name, every other channel (ads, referrals, AI) leaks visitors.
findings.fix: Use one consistent brand name everywhere, add Organization schema with alternateName, and build branded mentions.

findings.title: Far fewer pages indexed than crawled
findings.evidence: Google site: estimate 5 vs 88 crawlable pages
findings.why: Pages that are not indexed cannot rank. This is an estimate; confirm in Search Console.
findings.fix: Check Search Console → Pages for "Crawled – currently not indexed" and "Discovered – currently not indexed", improve internal links and content depth on those URLs.

findings.title: Articles have no named human author
findings.why: Expertise signals (E-E-A-T) depend on a real, credentialed author, especially on advice or compliance topics.
findings.fix: Credit a named expert with an author page, job title and LinkedIn (author @type Person with url and sameAs).

findings.title: Broken internal links
findings.why: Links to pages that no longer exist waste crawl budget and send users to dead ends.
findings.fix: Export the broken links from the crawl and fix or remove each one; redirect deleted pages to the closest live page.

findings.title: Few verified profiles linked in sameAs
findings.why: Entity recognition works best with 4-6 independent profiles (LinkedIn, directories, Wikidata, Crunchbase, review sites).
findings.fix: Add sameAs links to every real business profile.

findings.title: No freshness signal on articles
findings.evidence: 2 of 2 sampled articles have dateModified equal to datePublished
findings.why: Time-sensitive content looks unmaintained without a genuine update date.
findings.fix: Show a visible "Last reviewed" date and update dateModified only after real edits.

findings.title: Contact form is not in the server-rendered HTML
findings.evidence: Raw HTML of https://www.techand.ai/contact-us has 0 <form> and 0 <input> elements
findings.why: Crawlers and AI agents that do not run JavaScript see no way to contact you.
findings.fix: Server-render the form (fields, labels, submit) or add a <noscript> fallback form.

findings.title: Images without width and height
findings.evidence: 76 images on sampled pages lack explicit dimensions
findings.why: Images without reserved space can shift the layout while loading (CLS).
findings.fix: Add width and height (or aspect-ratio) to every image.

findings.title: No rankings for informational searches
findings.evidence: You rank for 0 informational keywords vs competitor median 234
findings.why: You are missing a whole stage of the buyer journey that competitors capture.
findings.fix: Publish helpful guides that answer the questions buyers research.

findings.title: High backlink spam score
findings.why: A high share of low-quality links can hold rankings back.
findings.fix: Review the worst linking domains and disavow clearly manipulative ones.

findings.title: Largest Contentful Paint needs improvement (2.5-4s)
findings.why: Google rates LCP above 2.5 seconds as Needs Improvement.
findings.fix: Speed up server response and optimise the main image.

findings.title: Service pages are generic and duplicated
findings.evidence: Every /whatwedo/ page repeats the same block: "We guide your business through every step of technology growth to ensure you stay ahead of competitors." Each page also carries the same "Assess & Envision" copy. Managed Services is described as "Expert IT management for your daily needs".
findings.why: Duplicated boilerplate and generic descriptions give each page little unique value. The pages lack timelines, deliverables and UAE specifics.
findings.fix: Write unique content per service: scope, methodology, typical timelines, deliverables, SLAs, a UAE example and FAQs.

findings.title: Heavy repeated mega-menu text on every page
findings.evidence: The same navigation text, from "Dynamics 365 Finance & Operations UAE" to "Predictive Models", precedes the content on every page.
findings.why: It dilutes the unique content, and the menu shows up as page text. Menu labels also look keyword-stuffed ("…UAE" repeated).
findings.fix: Make the navigation less crawlable-noisy and the labels more natural. Make sure the main content comes first in the HTML.

findings.title: Formatting artifact and only high-commitment CTAs
findings.evidence: "Let's discuss how we can help your business" shows a raw HTML entity. CTAs are "Talk to Sales", "Call Now" and "Request Call Back".
findings.why: The artifact looks unpolished. There is no low-friction option such as a guide, assessment or pricing guidance.
findings.fix: Fix the entity encoding. Add softer CTAs such as a readiness checklist, a sample scope or a downloadable guide.

findings.title: No pricing or engagement-model guidance, and no leadership info
findings.evidence: No pricing, ranges, or engagement models appear on the service pages. No team or leadership names appear in the text supplied.
findings.why: Buyers can't qualify the cost. Anonymity lowers trust.
findings.fix: Add indicative engagement models, typical project durations, and a leadership/team page.

findings.title: Google shows AI Overviews for your key searches and does not cite you
findings.evidence: "ai in cloud" (cited: aicloud.core42.ai, asus.com, youtube.com, nebius.com)
findings.why: These queries already have an AI answer; pages that are not cited lose visibility.
findings.fix: Add a concise answer block, question-style headings and primary-source citations on the relevant pages.

findings.title: Missing canonical tag
findings.why: Without a canonical, duplicate URL versions can compete with each other.
findings.fix: Add a self-referencing canonical tag to every indexable page.

findings.title: Canonical points to a redirect
findings.why: Mixed signals slow down consolidation of ranking signals.
findings.fix: Point canonicals directly to the final URL.

findings.title: No compression (gzip/brotli)
findings.why: Uncompressed pages take longer to download.
findings.fix: Enable gzip or brotli compression on the server.

findings.title: Large image payload (over 1MB of images per page)
findings.why: Large images are the most common cause of slow mobile pages. The figure is the total size of image files the page references (including responsive sizes), so the real download may be smaller, but it signals unoptimised images.
findings.fix: Compress images, serve WebP/AVIF, and make sure image CDN optimisation (e.g. f_auto,q_auto) is on.

findings.title: Structured data with errors
findings.why: Search engines ignore structured data blocks that fail validation, so the page loses rich-result eligibility.
findings.fix: Validate each page in the Rich Results Test / Schema Markup Validator and fix the reported properties.

findings.title: Brand name repeated in the title
findings.why: A doubled brand suffix wastes title space and usually means the template adds the brand twice.
findings.fix: Fix the title template so the brand appears once.
sample_urls: https://www.techand.ai/power-platform-analytics-uae — "Power Platform & Analytics Services in UAE | Tech& | Tech&"

findings.title: Missing security headers
findings.why: Security headers protect visitors. They are not a direct ranking factor but show a well-maintained site.
findings.fix: Add the missing headers in your hosting or CDN configuration; start Content-Security-Policy in Report-Only mode.

findings.title: No alternateName in Organization schema
findings.why: Helps search engines and AI map spelling variants of the brand to one entity.
findings.fix: Add alternateName with common variants of the brand name.

findings.title: Organization schema has no @id
findings.why: An @id lets other schema (Service, Article) reference the same organisation cleanly.
findings.fix: Add "@id": "https://techand.ai/#organization".

findings.title: Homepage H1 does not name the business or what it does
findings.evidence: Homepage H1: "Value Driven Innovation through Automation"
findings.why: The homepage H1 is the strongest on-page signal of who you are, what you sell and where.
findings.fix: Rewrite the H1 to name the brand, the service category and the location.

findings.title: Phone number in a link but not shown on the page
findings.why: Hidden or unlabeled numbers can be picked up by directories and AI as conflicting contact details.
findings.fix: Confirm the number, display it, or remove the link.

findings.title: No speculation rules for instant navigation
findings.why: Prefetching likely next pages makes navigation feel instant.
findings.fix: Add conservative speculation rules for key pages (e.g. contact and top services).

findings.title: Low-difficulty keywords you can target now
findings.evidence: "ai in cloud" (27100/mo, difficulty 12), "ai on cloud" (27100/mo, difficulty 10), "cloud's ai" (27100/mo, difficulty 28), "blackbox ai" (14800/mo, difficulty 15), "vertically" (9900/mo, difficulty 4)
findings.why: These searches have real demand and weak competition, the best starting point for a young site.
findings.fix: Build or optimise one focused page per keyword group, starting with the highest volume.

findings.title: Top speed-up opportunities
findings.why: Google lists these as the biggest savings available.
findings.fix: Work through these in order of estimated savings.

findings.title: Missing Open Graph tags
findings.why: Without them, links shared on LinkedIn, WhatsApp or Facebook show a poor preview.
findings.fix: Add og:title, og:description and og:image.

findings.title: URLs are not SEO-friendly
findings.why: Dynamic parameters, long paths or non-descriptive URLs are harder to read and share.
findings.fix: Use short, lowercase, hyphenated, descriptive URLs.

findings.title: Internal URLs that redirect
findings.why: Redirects add load time and dilute crawl efficiency.
findings.fix: Link directly to the final URL.

findings.title: Links pointing to redirects
findings.why: Extra hops for users and crawlers.
findings.fix: Update links to point to the final URL.

findings.title: Title shorter than 30 characters
findings.why: Short titles waste space to include keywords and a reason to click.
findings.fix: Expand to 50-60 characters with the main keyword and benefit.

findings.title: Long or messy URLs
findings.why: Long URLs, capitals or underscores are harder to read, share and remember.
findings.fix: Use short, lowercase, hyphenated URLs.

findings.title: Few internal links pointing to the page
findings.why: Pages with few internal links look less important to search engines.
findings.fix: Add contextual links from related pages with descriptive anchor text.

findings.title: Light content (300-500 words)
findings.why: Commercial pages usually need more depth to compete.
findings.fix: Expand with answers to the questions buyers ask before contacting you.

findings.title: Missing Twitter/X card tags
findings.why: Shared links on X show a plain preview.
findings.fix: Add twitter:card and twitter:image tags.

findings.title: Canonical points to a different page
findings.why: Fine if intentional, but this page will not rank on its own.
findings.fix: Confirm each of these is intentional.

findings.title: H1 is identical to the title tag
findings.why: A slightly different H1 lets you target a second keyword variation.
findings.fix: Optional: vary the H1 wording from the title.

site_audit.scoring_method: Full SEO health. Each category starts at 100. Findings written by the AI content review, and notes about data that could not be collected, are listed but do not change the score. Each other finding deducts Critical 30, High 15, Medium 7, Low 3, Info 1 points, scaled by the share of pages affected (60%-100% of the penalty); site-wide issues take the full penalty. Within a category, each further finding of the same severity counts 70% of the previous one, so many small issues cannot zero a category on their own. The score is the weighted average of category scores, capped at 70 with one critical issue, 60 with two or more, and 85 with five or more high-priority issues.
notes: AI crawler checks use the crawler user-agent only; real crawlers are also verified by IP, so a pass here means no user-agent based blocking.
Some extra crawl reports were unavailable: duplicate_title: Task Not Found.; duplicate_description: Task Not Found.; non_indexable: Task Not Found.; redirect_chains: Task Not Found.
